initiatives.name: Banking Operations Divestiture & Barclays Partnership
initiatives.summary: Tesco completed the sale of its Banking operations to Barclays and entered into an exclusive 10-year partnership providing customers with Tesco-branded banking products and services. The company retained insurance and money services activities including ATMs, travel money and gift cards.

evidence.title: Sale of Banking operations to Barclays completed
evidence.summary: Tesco completed the sale of its Banking operations to Barclays and entered into an exclusive 10-year partnership providing customers with Tesco-branded banking products and services. The company retained insurance and money services activities including ATMs, travel money and gift cards.
evidence.quote: the Board approved the sale of its Banking operations to Barclays and entered into an exclusive 10-year partnership providing customers with access to Tesco-branded banking products and services, combining Tesco's market-leading brand, physical and digital reach, and relentless customer focus with Barclays' deep financial services capabilities and expertise in commercial partnerships. Following the completion in November 2024, the Board announced its intention to return £700m to shareholders via an incremental share buyback.

evidence.title: Strategic Partnership with Barclays
evidence.summary: Tesco established a 10-year exclusive partnership with Barclays to provide Tesco-branded banking products and services. The partnership combines Tesco's retail reach with Barclays' financial services capabilities following the sale of Tesco's banking operations.
evidence.quote: The exclusive 10-year partnership provides customers access to Tesco-branded banking products and services, combining Tesco's market-leading brand, physical and digital reach and relentless customer focus with Barclays' deep financial services capabilities and expertise in commercial partnerships.

evidence.title: Sale of Banking Operations to Barclays
evidence.summary: Tesco completed the sale of its Banking operations to Barclays in November 2024 for gross proceeds of £614m. The company retained insurance business, ATMs, travel money and gift cards, and launched a strategic partnership with Barclays for Tesco-branded financial products.
evidence.quote: In November 2024, we completed the sale of our Banking operations to Barclays, while retaining our insurance business, ATMs, travel money and gift cards which will trade under the Tesco Insurance and Money Services brand. We also launched a new long-term strategic partnership with Barclays to provide our customers access to a range of Tesco-branded financial products

initiatives.name: Save to Invest Programme
initiatives.summary: Tesco delivered £510m efficiency savings for FY 24/25 through its save to invest programme. The programme focuses on simplifying operations, reducing costs, and creating headroom to fund investments across goods & services, operations, property and central overheads.

evidence.title: Save to Invest Programme Efficiency Savings
evidence.summary: Tesco delivered £510m efficiency savings for FY 24/25 through its save to invest programme. The programme focuses on simplifying operations, reducing costs, and creating headroom to fund investments across goods & services, operations, property and central overheads.
evidence.quote: Save to invest progress, delivering £510m of savings for FY 24/25. Continued progress across all areas, including goods & services not for resale, operations, property and central overheads.

evidence.title: New Robotic Automation at Distribution Centres
evidence.summary: Tesco implemented new robotic automation at its Peterborough distribution centre and has the Aylesford semi-automated distribution centre on track to open in summer 2025. This is part of their save to invest programme to automate the distribution network.
evidence.quote: New robotic automation implemented at our Peterborough distribution centre, with Aylesford semi-automated distribution centre on track to open in summer 2025.

initiatives.name: Share Buyback Programme
initiatives.summary: Tesco committed to buying back £1bn of shares by April 2025 (completed in February 2025) and intends to buy back a further £1.45bn by April 2026, with £700m funded by proceeds from the Tesco Bank sale. The sole purpose is to reduce share capital.

evidence.title: Share buyback programme commitment
evidence.summary: Tesco committed to buying back £1bn of shares by April 2025 (completed in February 2025) and intends to buy back a further £1.45bn by April 2026, with £700m funded by proceeds from the Tesco Bank sale. The sole purpose is to reduce share capital.
evidence.quote: On 10 April 2024, the Company committed to buying back an additional £1bn worth of shares by April 2025, of which £250m was funded by a one-off special dividend received from Tesco Bank. This tranche completed in February 2025. The Company intends to buy back a further £1.45bn by no later than April 2026, of which £700m will be funded by the proceeds of the sale of Tesco Bank during the financial year.

initiatives.name: Store Colleague Pay Investment
initiatives.summary: Tesco invested in its largest-ever increase in store colleague pay and improved benefits. The company is investing another £180m in colleague pay this year and has invested more than £900m in pay increases since April 2022.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £180m this year, more than £900m since April 2022

evidence.title: Largest Ever Store Colleague Pay Investment
evidence.summary: Tesco invested in its largest-ever increase in store colleague pay and improved benefits. The company is investing another £180m in colleague pay this year and has invested more than £900m in pay increases since April 2022.
evidence.quote: Over the past year, we invested in our largest-ever increase in store colleague pay and improved parental and wellbeing offerings. We are investing another £180m in colleague pay this year and have invested more than £900m in pay increases since April 2022.

initiatives.name: Store Network Expansion Programme
initiatives.summary: Tesco opened 90 new stores across the Group (64 in UK, 12 in ROI, 14 in Central Europe) and refreshed 463 stores. The company continues to invest in its physical store estate as part of its convenience strategy.

evidence.title: Store Network Expansion Programme
evidence.summary: Tesco opened 90 new stores across the Group (64 in UK, 12 in ROI, 14 in Central Europe) and refreshed 463 stores. The company continues to invest in its physical store estate as part of its convenience strategy.
evidence.quote: We have opened 90 new stores across the Group, Whoosh goes from strength to strength, and now offers delivery from a number of large stores. And while Booker has faced some challenging market conditions, we welcomed a further 566 net new retail partners, taking the total to just under 8,000.

initiatives.name: AI-Powered Clubcard Challenges
initiatives.summary: Tesco launched AI-powered Clubcard Challenges campaign to provide greater personalisation. More than 10 million customers were given the chance to earn up to £50 worth of Clubcard vouchers over Christmas through this AI initiative.

evidence.title: AI-Powered Clubcard Challenges Launch
evidence.summary: Tesco launched AI-powered Clubcard Challenges campaign to provide greater personalisation. More than 10 million customers were given the chance to earn up to £50 worth of Clubcard vouchers over Christmas through this AI initiative.
evidence.quote: The launch of our AI-powered Clubcard Challenges campaign amplified our efforts to give customers ever-greater personalisation, with more than 10 million given the chance to earn up to £50 worth of Clubcard vouchers over Christmas.

initiatives.name: Tesco Marketplace Launch
initiatives.summary: In June 2025, Tesco launched Tesco Marketplace offering customers a broader range of products online through third-party sellers. The platform now offers over 400,000 products with new category launches planned for FY 25/26.

evidence.title: Tesco Marketplace Launch
evidence.summary: In June 2025, Tesco launched Tesco Marketplace offering customers a broader range of products online through third-party sellers. The platform now offers over 400,000 products with new category launches planned for FY 25/26.
evidence.quote: In June, we launched Tesco Marketplace, offering customers an even broader range of products online through third-party sellers. We are now offering over 400,000 products and have built a pipeline of further sellers to join the platform, with new category launches planned for later in FY 25/26.

initiatives.name: Renewable Energy Power Purchase Agreements
initiatives.summary: Tesco signed new power purchase agreements for solar energy from Cleve Hill solar park (powering equivalent of 144 large stores) and wind energy from Stranoch windfarm (powering equivalent of 80 supermarkets). Combined with existing PPAs, this could cover 41% of Tesco UK electricity demand.

evidence.title: Solar and Wind Energy Power Purchase Agreements
evidence.summary: Tesco signed new power purchase agreements for solar energy from Cleve Hill solar park (powering equivalent of 144 large stores) and wind energy from Stranoch windfarm (powering equivalent of 80 supermarkets). Combined with existing PPAs, this could cover 41% of Tesco UK electricity demand.
evidence.quote: The signing of a new power purchase agreement ensures we'll receive enough solar energy from the Cleve Hill solar park to power the equivalent of 144 large stores every year – a tenth of our total electricity demand. A further deal for a windfarm at Stranoch will add clean energy for the equivalent of 80 average-sized supermarkets.

initiatives.name: Annual Capital Investment Programme
initiatives.summary: Tesco committed to significant capital expenditure across store refreshes, digital platforms, and automation. The company refreshed 463 stores and expects similar investment levels in FY 25/26.

evidence.title: Annual Capital Investment Programme
evidence.summary: Tesco committed to significant capital expenditure across store refreshes, digital platforms, and automation. The company refreshed 463 stores and expects similar investment levels in FY 25/26.
evidence.quote: Our total capital expenditure for the year was £1,457m, £143m higher year-on-year. Our capital expenditure for the year includes investing in our core assets, as well as investing in growth, such as our online customer proposition, and delivering efficiencies across our operations, including further automation within our distribution and fulfilment centres. We continue to see attractive opportunities to commit capital to high-returning investments, and expect a similar level of capital investment in FY 25/26.

initiatives.name: Non-Executive Director Appointment (Chris Kennedy)
initiatives.summary: Chris Kennedy joined the Board as Non-executive Director in February 2025, bringing financial management and strategic planning experience from his role as CFO and COO at ITV. He is a member of the Audit Committee and Nominations and Governance Committee.

evidence.title: New Non-Executive Director Appointment
evidence.summary: Chris Kennedy joined the Board as Non-executive Director in February 2025, bringing financial management and strategic planning experience from his role as CFO and COO at ITV. He is a member of the Audit Committee and Nominations and Governance Committee.
evidence.quote: In February, we welcomed Chris Kennedy to the Board as a Non-executive Director. As the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer at ITV, Chris brings a wealth of knowledge in financial management, strategic planning and corporate governance, and will be a real asset to the Board.

evidence.title: Chris Kennedy appointed Non-executive Director
evidence.summary: The Nominations Committee recommended and the Board appointed Chris Kennedy as a Non-executive Director. He also joined the Audit Committee to strengthen governance capabilities.
evidence.quote: The Committee recommended to the Board the appointment of Chris Kennedy who joined the Board as a Non-executive Director in February 2025.

initiatives.name: Group General Counsel Appointment
initiatives.summary: Kay Majid was permanently appointed as Group General Counsel and Executive Committee member in September 2024, replacing Adrian Morris who left after 11 years. Kay had been with Tesco for 15 years leading UK legal agenda.

evidence.title: New Group General Counsel Appointment
evidence.summary: Kay Majid was permanently appointed as Group General Counsel and Executive Committee member in September 2024, replacing Adrian Morris who left after 11 years. Kay had been with Tesco for 15 years leading UK legal agenda.
evidence.quote: In July, our Group General Counsel, Adrian Morris, left Tesco after a career of 11 years leading our Legal team and as a member of the Executive Committee. I was delighted to confirm the permanent appointment of Kay Majid as our Group General Counsel and member of the Executive Committee in September.

initiatives.name: Booker Catering Hubs Expansion
initiatives.summary: Investment in Booker has supported growing demand for delivery through opening new catering hubs, which has improved availability and customer satisfaction. This expansion addresses the evolving retail delivery market.

evidence.title: Booker catering hubs expansion investment
evidence.summary: Investment in Booker has supported growing demand for delivery through opening new catering hubs, which has improved availability and customer satisfaction. This expansion addresses the evolving retail delivery market.
evidence.quote: Investment in Booker has supported the growing demand for delivery with the opening of new catering hubs, improved availability and greater customer satisfaction.

initiatives.name: Healthcare Partnerships for Store Concept
initiatives.summary: Tesco partnered with leading UK healthcare companies to develop a new store concept providing customers with convenient access to high-quality health services. This leverages their network of stores and pharmacies across UK communities.

evidence.title: Healthcare partnerships for new store concept
evidence.summary: Tesco partnered with leading UK healthcare companies to develop a new store concept providing customers with convenient access to high-quality health services. This leverages their network of stores and pharmacies across UK communities.
evidence.quote: We have partnered with some of the UK's leading healthcare companies as part of a new store concept that gives customers easy and convenient access to even more high-quality health services. With our network of stores and pharmacies in communities all over the UK, we are uniquely placed to help make food and healthcare accessible to our customers.

initiatives.name: Robotic Automation Operational Efficiency
initiatives.summary: Tesco is investing in robotic automation to streamline operations, improve efficiency and support delivery of a seamless shopping experience for customers. This supports their longer-term strategic objectives through technology investments.

evidence.title: Robotic automation investment for operational efficiency
evidence.summary: Tesco is investing in robotic automation to streamline operations, improve efficiency and support delivery of a seamless shopping experience for customers. This supports their longer-term strategic objectives through technology investments.
evidence.quote: We continue to build our capabilities to support delivery of our longer-term objectives through investments in our people and technology, including robotic automation to streamline operations, improve efficiency and support our commitment to deliver a seamless shopping experience for our customers.

initiatives.name: Data Analytics and AI in Audit Processes
initiatives.summary: Tesco's internal audit team is expanding use of data analytics, continuous monitoring and artificial intelligence to analyze large volumes of data, identify trends and provide greater insights and assurance. The external auditor has also outlined a five-year plan focusing on enhancing efficiency through data analytics and AI.

evidence.title: Data analytics and AI integration in audit processes
evidence.summary: Tesco's internal audit team is expanding use of data analytics, continuous monitoring and artificial intelligence to analyze large volumes of data, identify trends and provide greater insights and assurance. The external auditor has also outlined a five-year plan focusing on enhancing efficiency through data analytics and AI.
evidence.quote: The Group's internal audit team has expanded its use of data analytics, to allow it to analyse large volumes of data quickly and accurately, identifying trends, anomalies, and potential risks that might not be visible through traditional audit methods. AI technologies, such as machine learning and natural language processing, can automate routine audit tasks, enhance risk assessment and provide predictive insights.
